item.text:
**7B.6 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**
Assessment: **mixed, leaning negative**. Marcos tolerated some domestic procedural scrutiny, but he did **not** tolerate full external scrutiny of the drug war, and the broader environment for independent investigation of power, money, and allies remained weak.

- **PBBM says Comelec has mandate to probe alleged signature-buying for PI** — *Philippine News Agency*, January 23, 2024. URL: [https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217440](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217440)  
  Marcos said he would not meddle with Comelec’s inquiry into alleged signature-buying in the people’s initiative drive, which is a real sign of procedural deference to an independent election body.  
  QIDs: **7B.6, 7B.3**

- **PBBM: ICC issue is about jurisdiction, not evidence on drug war** — *Philippine News Agency*, February 20, 2024. URL: [https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1219179](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1219179)  
  Marcos said the ICC could gather evidence and that the Philippines was an “open country,” but he still rejected ICC jurisdiction. This is mixed evidence: he did not fully block investigators, but he would not open his administration to meaningful external judicial scrutiny.  
  QIDs: **7B.6**

- **Philippines: Supreme Court Rejects ‘Red-Tagging’** — *Human Rights Watch*, May 8, 2024. URL: [https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/08/philippines-supreme-court-rejects-red-tagging](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/08/philippines-supreme-court-rejects-red-tagging)  
  The Supreme Court ruled red-tagging is a threat to life, liberty, and security. In the 2024 record I reviewed, Marcos did not retaliate against that ruling, which is modest evidence that he tolerated at least some judicial constraint.  
  QIDs: **7B.6, 7B.2**

- **DOJ eyes conspiracy, sedition, other graver charges vs. VP Duterte, hired killers** — *Presidential Communications Office*, November 25, 2024. URL: [https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/doj-eyes-conspiracy-sedition-other-graver-charges-vs-vp-duterte-hired-killers/](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/doj-eyes-conspiracy-sedition-other-graver-charges-vs-vp-duterte-hired-killers/)  
  The DOJ said legal remedies and due process would be used in the probe tied to death threats against Marcos, with other agencies involved in identifying suspects. This shows the administration was willing to pursue some formal investigations, but it is about threats to Marcos rather than scrutiny of Marcos himself.  
  QIDs: **7B.6**

- **No PH cooperation with ICC unless PRRD wants it – PBBM** — *Presidential Communications Office*, November 14, 2024. URL: [https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/no-ph-cooperation-with-icc-unless-prrd-wants-it-pbbm/](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/no-ph-cooperation-with-icc-unless-prrd-wants-it-pbbm/)  
  Marcos explicitly said the Philippines would not cooperate with the ICC probe into the Duterte drug war unless Duterte allowed it. That is the clearest negative evidence: he tolerated only a narrow, controlled form of review and refused independent international investigation.  
  QIDs: **7B.6**

- **Philippines: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report** — *Freedom House*, 2024. URL: [https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024)  
  Freedom House says campaign-finance rules were weak and poorly enforced, and that patronage and kinship still shaped political power. That is strong background evidence that independent investigation of money, donors, and conflicts of interest was structurally hard in 2024.  
  QIDs: **7B.6, 7B.4**

- **Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism** — *Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism*, June 17, 2024. URL: [https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines)  
  The report describes persistent red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and political pressure over broadcasters, alongside politically connected business moves involving the Romualdez family. This is indirect but important evidence that independent scrutiny of associates and concealed decisions still faced a coercive environment.  
  QIDs: **7B.6, 7B.4, 7B.5**

- **Sandiganbayan junks P276-M ill-gotten wealth case vs Marcos family, associate** — *GMA News Online*, October 9, 2024. URL: [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/923067/sandiganbayan-ill-gotten-wealth-marcos-family/story/](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/923067/sandiganbayan-ill-gotten-wealth-marcos-family/story/)  
  An independent asset-recovery case involving the Marcos family and an associate was dismissed due to inordinate delay, not because Marcos opened up his assets to scrutiny. This is relevant mainly as a gap signal: there was litigation, but not evidence of Marcos welcoming or facilitating full accountability.  
  QIDs: **7B.6, 7B.4**

**Search gap:** I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Marcos voluntarily opened his own SALNs, private assets, donor records, or internal conflict-of-interest decisions to independent audit or public review. The strongest material is indirect: he allowed some domestic procedures to run, but he blocked ICC cooperation and the broader transparency environment remained constrained.
